name: The Equitable Life Insurance Company of Canada (Equitable)
ownership: Mutual (owned by participating policyholders); no listed securities

metrics.note: +24% y/y (C$10.21bn at YE2024). General fund C$7.90bn + segregated funds C$4.80bn. No interim financials published (mutual, annual reporting only).
Bonds 2,734; equities 2,533; private placements 853; investment property 545; mortgages 518; cash/ST 61; derivatives 14; seed capital 6 (C$mm). C$6.29bn at YE2024.
+43% y/y (C$3.36bn YE2024); Individual Wealth deposits C$1.82bn in 2025. No separate AUM/AUMA measure published; brochure cites 'C$12.7bn of assets under administration' (= total assets).
FY2024 C$186.9mm. All income attributed to participating policyholders' equity. No core/underlying earnings measure; no YTD 2026 figure published.
+27% y/y. Policyholder dividends paid C$176mm; claims and benefits C$1.62bn.

169% YE2024, 172% YE2023 (174% at Q1 2024 per DBRS). Capital resources C$3,208mm vs base solvency buffer C$2,018mm. Internal target not disclosed. Total balance sheet capital C$2,405mm (policyholders' equity 1,733 + CSM 672).
No debt, preferred shares or hybrids outstanding (DBRS: 'no debt outstanding'; FS show no borrowings).
FSR A (high), Issuer Rating A (high), Stable trends; upgraded to A (high) Sept 2020. AR 2025 (Feb 2026) states DBRS confirmed A (high) Stable. No AM Best, S&P or Moody's ratings.
Not disclosed. In-house 'Asset Management division' led by EVP & CIO; job postings reference a VP Private Investments and credit team (Waterloo). Team page not published.
'More than 1,400 employees across the country' (company brochure). Canada's Top 100 Employers listing shows 1,084 FT + 42 PT (undated).

pm_structure.summary: In-house Asset Management division (bottom-up credit, active duration, ETFs for public equity) manages the general account; external funds for PE, infrastructure equity and part of real estate; no affiliated manager.
manager_entities: Equitable Asset Management division (in-house; CIO Eugene Lundrigan)
External fund managers: PE (buyout, co-invest, mezzanine, secondaries), infrastructure equity (4 managers from 2025), property funds
Third-party fund managers underlying segregated funds / GIFs (inferred)
bullets: Strategic asset allocation per portfolio with active tilts; own credit research for bonds, private placements and commercial mortgages
Public equity via ETFs; preferred shares IG-focused for tax-advantaged dividends
Investment property direct and via external funds; commercial mortgages originated in-house (LTV to 75%, CMHC-insured above)
Oversight: Asset Management Committee and Board Investment Committee; custodian is securities-lending agent with borrower indemnity
GF managed assets (AR p.11): bonds 38%, public equity 26%, private placements 12%, property 8%, mortgages 7%, prefs 6%, PE 2%, other 1%

rotation_commentary.text: 2025: initiated infrastructure equity via four fund commitments with four external managers; build-out continues in 2026 across geography, strategy, sector.
2025: private placements +38% to C$853mm, mortgages +19% to C$518mm, property +19% to C$545mm; public bonds flat at C$2.73bn.
2025: corporates 65% of bond book (60% in 2024); governments used for liquidity/duration; new Equitable GIFs launched Nov 2025.
2024 AR: close to 60% of private-placement energy exposure is renewable (solar, wind, hydro, biogas); mortgages include affordable rental housing.

target_allocations.target: Not published; AR states a strategic asset allocation is set per portfolio and actively managed around it

debt_outstanding.type: None - no senior, subordinated, LRCN, preferred or hybrid capital outstanding
debt_outstanding.note: Mutual; capital = participating policyholders' equity C$1,733mm + CSM C$672mm

securities_lending.text: Securities loaned C$898.1mm (C$968.9mm at YE2024) against collateral of C$1,026.3mm (C$1,045.8mm); custodian is lending agent, marks daily and indemnifies borrower default. Loaned securities remain in invested assets.

repos.text: No repurchase or reverse repurchase agreements disclosed. Derivative collateral: C$0.3mm bonds pledged, nil held (CSA with major Canadian bank counterparties); derivatives C$14.5mm assets.

structured_indirect.text: Private placements (illiquid private fixed income with covenants/collateral; includes infrastructure such as port, rail, school-bus and renewables)
Commercial mortgages (office, retail, multi-family, industrial; uninsured up to 75% LTV)
Private equity funds (~2% of general fund managed assets) and infrastructure equity funds (4 commitments, 2025); amounts and undrawn commitments not disclosed
No CLO/ABS, fund finance, SRT, sidecar or funding-agreement exposure disclosed

deals.text: Partnership with Empathy for enhanced loss/bereavement support (Mar 2026); RxFood added to all group benefits plans at no cost (Mar 2026)
New Equitable GIFs (Nov 2025); EVP & CIO hired from SLC Management (Sep 2025); EVP Strategy & Impact (Carbell) and EVP Individual Insurance (Reeves) named Mar 2025
CEO succession: Fabien Jeudy (ex-Sun Life Hong Kong) succeeded Ronald Beettam (July 2021)

sponsorships.text: The Equitable Foundation: C$500,000 in donations to food-insecurity charities (Jul 2026); 2025 Impact Report released May 2026
C$4.6mm donation to Waterloo Region health care (centennial)

bank_relationships.text: No bank ownership or bancassurance; distributes through independent advisors and MGAs. Derivative counterparties are major Canadian financial institutions under credit support agreements.

appetite: Take risks only if aligned with purpose and creating long-term sustainable value for clients; understand impact on clients, partners, financial strength and reputation
Investment and lending policies set eligible assets, diversification and exposure/concentration/quality limits; equity mostly backs par/UL pass-through
Reinsurance placed only with counterparties rated A or better
governance: Board with Audit, Conduct Review, Governance/Compliance/Nominating, HR & Compensation and Investment Committees (independent directors)
Senior Risk and Capital Committee and Asset Management Committee at management level; Appointed Actuary owns valuation assumptions
Three lines: business/corporate functions; CRO, Chief Compliance Officer, Chief Actuary, Head of Technology Risk; Internal Audit
risk.capital_target: Internal target not disclosed; LICAT 159% at YE2025 (OSFI supervisory 100%). Annual 5-year FCT confirmed resilience to adverse scenarios (2025).
sensitivities: Equity -10% / -35%: net income and equity -C$41.8mm / -C$146.2mm (YE2025); symmetric upside
Interest rates -50bp: net income -C$2.8mm, CSM -C$4.8mm; +50bp: net income -C$1.2mm, CSM +C$2.6mm (YE2025)
FX -10%: net income -C$10.2mm; investment property -10%: net income -C$21.2mm (YE2025)
Insurance: 2% mortality, 5% morbidity, 10% lapse and 5% expense sensitivities disclosed in FS note 10 (amounts in AR)
hedging: Asset-liability management program manages rate mismatch; derivatives (C$14.5mm FV) with Canadian bank counterparties under CSAs
Seg fund minimum death/maturity guarantees reserved in general fund; no dynamic hedging program described
Equity backing par/UL passes through to policyholders via dividend scale / credited rates, limiting shareholder-equivalent exposure
events: 2025: LICAT fell to 159% from 169% as capital resources now include seg-fund amounts under updated OSFI rules and growth consumed buffer
2025: CIO transition (Proper retired; Lundrigan hired from SLC Management); 2025 Board refresh (4 retirements, 2 additions)
DBRS A (high) confirmed Aug 2024 and (per AR) in 2025; no regulatory actions disclosed

gaps: Mutual company: no proxy circular; no executive compensation disclosed for any officer
No interim (Q1-Q3 2026) financial statements or capital ratio published; latest data is FY2025 (Feb 2026)
